explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/466: with N(X,δ) the maximum number of points in a disc of radius X whose pairwise distances are all at least δ from the nearest integer, is there δ > 0 with N(X,δ) → ∞? (yes, Graham; Sárközy). The Lean N X δ is the sSup of sizes of finite point sets in some closed ball of radius X with pairwise distToNearestInt(dist) ≥ δ; for δ > 0 such sets are δ-separated in a bounded region, so sizes are bounded and sSup is the maximum. The statement ∃ δ > 0 with N(X,δ) → ∞ as X → ∞ is a direct transcription. Faithful.
